variants.prompt:
Real interior photograph, 4:3 landscape, of one piece of custom-made furniture installed in a Romanian apartment. The attached 3D render shows the piece: use it ONLY as the geometry and colour reference. The furniture in the photo must match the render exactly in proportions, number of doors, drawers and compartments, colours and handles; everything else (room, light, materials) must be a real photograph.
Piece: Floor-standing wardrobe 240 cm wide × 260 cm high × 60 cm deep with exactly 3 full-height sliding doors of equal width (overlapping slightly, running on a slim top and bottom track), on a 10 cm recessed plinth. Real size 240 × 260 × 60 cm (width × height × depth).
Colours: body (side panels, top and plinth) in premium white melamine (Egger W1000 ST9: clean neutral white, fine matt pearl texture, not glossy, not bluish). Fronts (the 3 sliding door panels) in Natural Halifax oak (Egger H1180 ST37: warm honey-gold oak decor with visible cracks, knots and a deep tactile grain). Wood grain direction as in the render. (Colour combination „Alb & stejar natur".)
Handles: Sliding doors: no handles at all, only the slim vertical edge of each door.
Room: Bedroom (dormitor) of a Romanian apartment. Against a full wall of the bedroom, pushed into the corner so one side touches the side wall; the top ends about 10 cm below a 2.70 m ceiling. A double bed stands parallel to it with an 80–90 cm passage; nothing in front of the doors. Never in front of the window, radiator or room door. Ceiling height 2.70 m. The piece stands on the floor, tight against the wall, never floating.
Scene for this photo: The wardrobe stands on the wall opposite the window; the foot of a double bed with plain linen bedding enters the frame at lower left, a small wool rug beside it. Room surfaces: walls painted light warm grey; pale grey-beige laminate floor (clearly different from the oak fronts). Light: soft overcast daylight from a window on the left, neutral white balance.
Camera: Camera at 1.35–1.45 m height, 24–28 mm full-frame equivalent, standing 3.5–4 m back, three-quarter view about 20–30° off the wardrobe wall; verticals perfectly straight (corrected like an architectural shot), no fisheye, no wide-angle stretching at the edges. 4:3 landscape. The whole wardrobe is visible from plinth to top with a strip of ceiling above and floor below; it fills about 60–65% of the frame.
Photorealism: this must look like a real photograph of installed furniture taken by an interior photographer in a lived-in Romanian apartment, not a 3D render and not a catalogue illustration. Real melamine chipboard with matching 1–2 mm edge banding visible on the edges, even 2–3 mm gaps between fronts, true-to-scale 18 mm panel thickness, soft contact shadows under and beside the piece, faint natural reflections, slight real-life imperfection (a wall socket and light switch at normal heights, white skirting board, a radiator or door frame where it belongs). Believable scale: standard interior doors are 2.05 m high, sockets at 30 cm, switches at 1.05 m.
